challenges.finding: Contact follow-up is 69.0% in Tshopo; strike, aggression and threats disrupt surveillance. Two of three Ituri PoC suspects were not transferred because of ambulance unavailability or refusal. Butuhe remains closed.

Ituri reports 38 critically ill patients and a blood stockout. Nord-Kivu reports 22 critically ill patients and 154 patients outside CTE/CT. Two confirmed patients remain missing after leaving Bafwasende.

Nord-Kivu reports no kits for 13 decontaminated households and 40 postponed safe burials. Tshopo reports six of six bodies not swabbed. Bas-Uele reports 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage and 17 of 20 without 72-hour water supplies.
Vaccination remains research or compassionate activity, without demonstrated BDBV efficacy. Ituri reports 1,969 vaccinated; Bas-Uele reports 1,907 of 13,202 targeted (14.4%) and UCC not operational.
Maboya and Matanda assessments report no emergency service and insufficient PPE and blood products. In Tshopo, 22 PPL interrupted prophylaxis because of insecurity.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 15 of 28 affected zones. Ten affected Nord-Kivu zones lack nurseries. Wanie-Rukula support teams lack training, communications and mobility. Isiro, Pawa, Wamba and Boma Mangbetu have no nursery. Pillar case cohorts are not daily incidence.

Tshopo treatment-centre construction and extension continue, with 115 motorcycles still missing. Bas-Uele construction and office rehabilitation continue, with 140 litres of diesel, computers, printers and scanners missing.
Only two of eight provincial directorates reported PSEA activities. The reporting mechanism is known in five of 34 Nord-Kivu zones. Distinct pillar populations are not summed.

priorities: Strengthen early detection, contact follow-up and safe burials; source recommendation, not completion.
